clue.text: Dickensian letters induced alternative go-slow

parts.note: Litt. is the abbreviation for letters, as in the degree Litt.D., Doctor of Letters
to induce someone is to lead them on, so induced means led
or introduces an alternative
rit., short for ritardando, is the musical direction to slow down

explanation.surface: Correspondence from a Dickens character provoked a different kind of industrial slowdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go-slow' suggests industrial action but is a musical marking: RIT for ritardando. 'Dickensian' as a definition means a work by Dickens.
explanation.definitionFit: The novel of the Marshalsea debtors' prison is one of Charles Dickens's major works, hence a Dickensian title.

clue.text: Backbone needed by Campbell, an amateur in the city

parts.note: read as back plus bone: the bone word rib written backwards
Ming is the nickname of Sir Menzies Campbell, the Liberal Democrat politician
a ham is an amateur, especially a radio enthusiast

explanation.surface: A politician called Campbell needs some backbone when in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: The one word 'Backbone' does two things at once: 'back' turns round the bone it names. Menzies Campbell, a former Liberal Democrat leader, was known as Ming.
explanation.definitionFit: England's second city, in the West Midlands, is a classic example of a city.

clue.text: Revolutionary on board fixed it with men

parts.note: Che Guevara is the crossword's stock revolutionary
SS, steamship, is the usual frame for being on board
set means fixed, as in set in place

explanation.surface: A revolutionary on a ship fixed something with the help of the crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it with men' is a cryptic definition: the board and pieces (men) used for the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess pieces are traditionally called men, so the complete game kit is a thing that comes with men.

clue.text: Do 80th birthday repasts include such starters and leftovers?

indicators.note: starters signals the opening letters of the six words before it, with 80th read as the word eightieth

explanation.surface: A question about whether a big birthday meal includes such openers and remnants.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 80th as the word 'eightieth' to get its starter E. Araucaria was 85 at the time, a sly joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is scattered remains, the bits left over after something is broken or used up.

clue.text: Drops put underground in the West Riding

parts.note: dews are drops of moisture
to bury is to put underground

explanation.surface: Drops put underground somewhere in Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: The West Riding was one of the historic divisions of Yorkshire; Dewsbury is a town there.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition reads as a place found within the old West Riding of Yorkshire, a description of the Yorkshire town.

clue.text: Chilean soldier and outlaw controlled rebel uprising with traps

indicators.note: in a down entry uprising reads the soldier, outlaw, controlled and rebel run from bottom to top

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
Robin Hood is the archetypal outlaw
ran means controlled, as in ran a business
Reb is short for a Confederate rebel
gins are traps or snares

explanation.surface: A Chilean military man and an outlaw led a revolt that used traps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chilean soldier' looks like the definition, but soldier is GI; the definition is just 'Chilean'. 'uprising' turns GI+HOOD+RAN+REB into BERNARDOOHIG.
explanation.definitionFit: Bernardo O'Higgins led Chile to independence and was its first head of state, so a famous Chilean.

clue.text: Approaching solicitor on the tiles?

parts.note: nigh means near or approaching
a tout solicits custom, so is a solicitor

explanation.surface: A lawyer coming nearer, apparently walking about on a roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' suggests a lawyer but means someone who solicits. 'On the tiles' is British slang for out partying.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the tiles is an idiom for a spree of evening revelry, which is what an evening's outing amounts to.

clue.text: Emperor of pothooks

indicators.note: of says the answer is drawn from within the word pothooks

explanation.surface: An emperor found among some old handwriting strokes.
explanation.walkthrough: Pothooks are curved strokes in handwriting practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Otho ruled briefly as Roman emperor in AD 69, the Year of the Four Emperors.

clue.text: Sponsor of art ultimately was consumer

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word art

parts.note: ate is what someone who was a consumer did

explanation.surface: A patron of the arts was at last a consumer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate galleries carry the name of Henry Tate, the sugar magnate who funded the first one; 'of art' leads the eye to the definition and supplies the wordplay too.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar refiner Henry Tate paid for the London gallery that bears his name, so the family name stands for a benefactor.

clue.text: Passion in fighting time's not on

parts.note: war is fighting

indicators.note: not says the following word on is removed from the time period

parts.note: a month is a period of time
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ardour in battle, when there is no time for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes ON from MONTH, leaving MTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Warmth of feeling is ardour or passion, a common figurative synonym.

clue.text: His maths produces major success

indicators.note: produces suggests the letters of His maths are made into something new

explanation.surface: A student's maths work turns out to be a triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: A smash hit is a huge popular success, especially a show or record.

clue.text: O brother! a setback in decompression problem such as possessor can cash

indicators.note: in puts the reversed run inside the divers' illness

parts.note: the bends is decompression sickness suffered by divers

indicators.note: setback says the run O, brother, a is read backwards

parts.note: Brer is the dialect form of brother, as in Brer Rabbit

explanation.surface: A diver's lament about a setback, followed by talk of cashing something in.
explanation.walkthrough: Brer is the Uncle Remus spelling of brother (Brer Rabbit), so 'O brother! a' becomes a run of three pieces, and 'setback' turns that run round before it goes into the divers' ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: These securities are payable to whoever holds them, so any possessor can redeem them for cash.

clue.text: Abused race harmed — it's strictly for the birds

indicators.note: harmed suggests the letters of Abused race are damaged into a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint that an abused race was harmed, which some think nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the birds' means worthless, but here literally: the sauce is served with roast chicken or turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: This bread-thickened sauce is the traditional accompaniment to roast poultry, so literally meant for birds.

clue.text: Hot food fairy queen served up in coastal castle

indicators.note: in a down entry served up reads the hot, food and fairy queen run from bottom to top

parts.note: grub is slang for food
Queen Mab is the fairy queen in Romeo and Juliet

explanation.surface: A hot meal and a fairy queen are served at a seaside castle.
explanation.walkthrough: Bamburgh Castle stands on the Northumberland coast in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Bamburgh is a fortress perched on the North Sea shore, a clear instance of a castle by the sea.

clue.text: Bird slips aside into whisk

indicators.note: into puts the slips letters inside the whisk

parts.note: a beater is a kitchen whisk
E.E., errors excepted, sets aside any slips, as Chambers has it

explanation.surface: A bird slides sideways into a kitchen utensil.
explanation.walkthrough: E.E. (errors excepted) is a disclaimer on invoices: it puts slips to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: The bee-eater is a brightly coloured bird that catches bees and wasps in flight.

clue.text: Wine with bouquet a comic symbol?

parts.note: red is wine
a wine's nose is its bouquet

explanation.surface: A wine with a fine aroma, cast as a funny emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: The plastic red nose is the emblem of Comic Relief, a British charity telethon.
explanation.definitionFit: A clown's red nose is the badge of comedy and of the Comic Relief charity.

clue.text: See 5
Sea food that's grabbed over the counter was a good seller

indicators.note: that's grabbed says the fish holds the counter abbreviation inside it

parts.note: hake is a sea fish eaten as food
OTC is the abbreviation for over the counter

explanation.surface: Seafood snatched across a shop counter was selling well.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the idiom 'sold like hot cakes': a good seller went like this.
explanation.definitionFit: From the idiom selling like hot cakes, the treat stands for anything that sold quickly and well.

clue.text: Home — half of it with furniture — that can't be got down

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: half of takes the front four letters of the eight-letter word for home

parts.note: it refers back to home, here taken as a domicile
a table is an item of furniture

explanation.surface: A home half furnished cannot be brought low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home' gives IN, and 'it' points back to home again, now DOMICILE, of which 'half of' takes DOMI.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unconquerable cannot be subdued or brought down by any force.

clue.text: Hot line? Theme's about right

indicators.note: about says the theme goes around the right letter

parts.note: a topic is a theme; the 's means has

explanation.surface: A remark that a subject is almost correct.
explanation.walkthrough: The tropics are the lines of latitude bounding the hot zone of the Earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Each tropic is a line of latitude enclosing the torrid zone, hence a line with heat.

clue.text: Murphy with his alternative lawman turning up for love

indicators.note: for marks the turned word as standing in place of the love letter

parts.note: Sod's Law is a variant of Murphy's Law, so Sod is Murphy's alternative lawman
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: turning says the word up is read backwards

explanation.surface: Murphy and a rival law officer turn up instead of romance.
explanation.walkthrough: Sod's Law ('if it can go wrong, it will') is the British name for Murphy's Law.
explanation.definitionFit: Murphy is slang for a potato, from the Irish association; spud is another informal name for it.

clue.text: Nearly walk? Take the car

indicators.note: nearly says the walk word stops just short of its final letter

parts.note: to tramp is to walk heavily or a long way

explanation.surface: Almost walking, someone decides to drive instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A tram, or tramcar, is a passenger car that runs on rails along streets.

clue.text: Cold store reported by Scotsman to person from Asia Minor

indicators.note: reported says the cold store is heard rather than written

parts.note: a fridge stores food cold
Ian is a typical Scottish name

explanation.surface: A Scotsman reports a cold store to someone from Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrygia was an ancient kingdom in Asia Minor, so a native of it was from there.

clue.text: See 1
Island to suit small transport when docked

parts.note: do means suit, as in that will do

indicators.note: docked says the minicab loses its tail letter

parts.note: a minicab is a small hired car

explanation.surface: An island where a small cab is suitable once it is moored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' suggests a ship in port but means cut short, as with a tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominica is a Caribbean island nation in the Lesser Antilles.

clue.text: St John provided backing to silence Queen

indicators.note: backing says the provided word is turned round

parts.note: if means provided, as in provided that
sh is a call for silence
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A saint agreed to back the silencing of a queen.
explanation.walkthrough: St John Fisher was executed by Henry VIII for refusing to accept him as head of the Church, so the queen-silencing surface fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint John Fisher was the Bishop of Rochester martyred in 1535 and canonised in 1935.
